tools.summary: Combine PDFs, extract pages, or turn images into a PDF.
tools.description: Merge PDF files, split or extract pages, and convert JPG/PNG to PDF free. No sign-up, no watermark, no upload: everything runs in your browser.
features: Extract or split pages by range
Save each page as its own PDF
No upload: runs in the browser
tools.processing: in-browser (files and text are not uploaded)
how_to: Choose a task: merge, extract/split, or images to PDF.
Select your files (PDFs or images).
Click the button and download the result.

faq.q: How should I merge, split, or turn scans into a PDF for a real job?
faq.a: Merge joins files in the order you select them, so name the pieces or select them from first page to last. A contract plus an exhibit should be the contract file first. Split uses a page list such as 1-3, 5 to keep those pages, and Save each page writes one PDF per page when you need to file them separately. Images to PDF places each JPG or PNG on its own page in selection order, which is the right path for phone photos of a receipt stack. There is no fixed page cap. Very large files are limited by the memory of the device because the bytes never go to a server.

faq.q: Which PDF jobs belong together, and which do not?
faq.a: Merging is for documents that should travel as one file: a proposal and its appendix, or a set of signed pages. Splitting is for the opposite, when a portal wants one page or you must remove a page you did not mean to scan. Image-to-PDF is for pictures, not for editing the words inside an existing PDF. This tool does not reorder pages inside a file with a drag handle, rewrite text, OCR a scan into selectable words, or compress a PDF the way the image compressor shrinks a photo. If you need a smaller PDF, shrink the images first, then build the PDF.

faq.q: Why do some PDFs fail or come out blank?
faq.a: Password-protected files fail or produce blank pages because the page cannot decrypt them. Remove the password in a reader you are allowed to use, then merge the unlocked file. A truncated download or a file that is only named .pdf will also fail; the page tells you when the file does not look like a PDF. Browser memory is the other limit. Close extra tabs and merge in batches if a few hundred photo pages stall. The result is a normal PDF, not a PDF/A archival file and not a certified signed original. Printing to PDF again can flatten annotations.

faq.q: What are practical file-size and print targets?
faq.a: A packet you will email should usually stay under a few megabytes. Phone photos dropped straight into a PDF are often several megabytes each. Compress those images to about 1600 pixels on the long side at roughly 75 percent JPEG quality before you convert them to PDF, and a ten-page receipt packet becomes something you can attach. For a packet you will print, 200 to 300 pixels per inch at the printed size is enough for text and ordinary photos. A full-page photo at 300 DPI is about 2550 by 3300 pixels; you do not need a 48-megapixel original in the PDF.

faq.q: How do I keep client documents private and in order?
faq.a: The work runs in the browser with pdf-lib. Files are not uploaded to GWB and there is no account. That also means there is no cloud trash can: download the result before you close the tab, and keep your own copy of the originals. Do not merge documents you are not allowed to combine, and do not assume a merged file is still the signed original if you changed page order. A checksum or the file size in your download folder is a simple way to confirm the file finished writing.

faq.q: What should I do when the page list does not match the document?
faq.a: Page numbers in the box are PDF page indexes starting at 1, not the printed number in a footer. A file whose first page is numbered 12 is still page 1 in the box. Open the source and count if the footer and the index disagree. Ranges cannot invent pages past the end of the file. If you need pages from two files, merge first or split each file and then merge the pieces. The tool will not silently drop a password prompt and pretend the merge worked.

tools.name: Image Compressor & Resizer
tools.summary: Shrink JPG, PNG and WEBP images and resize them for the web.
tools.description: Compress and resize JPG, PNG and WEBP images free in your browser. No sign-up, no upload, no watermark and no file limits.
features: No upload: runs in the browser
tools.processing: in-browser (files and text are not uploaded)
how_to: Choose an image from your device.
Set the maximum width and quality, and pick JPG, WEBP or PNG.
Download the compressed image and compare the size savings.

faq.q: What width and quality should I use for web, email, and print?
faq.a: The width box is a maximum. A 6000-pixel photo set to 1600 pixels wide is scaled down and the height follows, so a 3:2 photo becomes about 1600 by 1067. The default quality is 75 percent, which is the right start for photographs on a website. At 1600 pixels and 75 percent JPEG, a multi-megabyte camera file often lands between about 150 and 400 KB. Use about 1080 pixels for an Instagram post, about 1200 for an email body, and about 400 for a thumbnail. For a hero image you will also print, keep a separate full-size original. This compressor is for screens. A logo you will print belongs in SVG or a PNG at the print size, not a 75 percent JPEG.

faq.q: Why did the file get larger, or why did a PNG barely shrink?
faq.a: PNG is lossless. Photographs stored as PNG stay large because the format cannot throw away the detail JPEG and WEBP discard. Switch the output to JPG or WEBP for photos. Logos, screenshots, and images with flat color and sharp edges should stay PNG or WEBP lossless so text does not grow halos. If a JPEG comes out larger than the original, the original was already compressed harder than your quality setting. Lower the quality or the width. The status line shows original size, new size, and the percent change so you can compare before you download.

faq.q: What happens to transparency, color, and EXIF?
faq.a: Choosing JPG fills transparent pixels with white before encoding, because JPEG has no alpha channel. A logo on a transparent background will grow a white box. Use PNG or WEBP if you need the transparency. The browser encoder also drops most camera metadata, including GPS, as a side effect of redrawing the pixels onto a canvas. That is useful when you do not want a location in a file you post, and it is a reason to keep the original if you still need the metadata. Animated GIFs are not preserved as animations; the page draws a bitmap.

faq.q: How do I hit a real target, such as a 200 KB product photo?
faq.a: Start at 1600 pixels and 75 percent. If you are still over the target, drop quality in 5 to 10 point steps or cut the width to 1200. Product photos on a white background often compress further than foliage or night scenes. Do not upscale. If the original is 800 pixels wide, a 1600 maximum leaves it at 800. Upscaling would invent pixels and usually a larger file. The preview is the file you will download. Judge edges and skin tones there, not by the percentage alone.

faq.q: Is this safe for client photos?
faq.a: Yes for privacy: the file is decoded and encoded in your browser and is not uploaded. There is no account and no library of your past images on our side. The limit is your device. An image whose pixel count is extreme is refused so the tab does not crash, and a 50 MB cap rejects a file that is unlikely to be a normal photo. Download the result; the object URL disappears when you leave. Keep the camera original somewhere else before you overwrite it.

faq.q: WEBP or JPG for a small-business site?
faq.a: WEBP is usually smaller than JPEG at the same visual quality and is supported by current browsers. JPEG is the safer attachment when the recipient is a mail program or a marketplace that rejects WEBP. A practical pair is WEBP for the site and JPEG for the marketplace upload. This page writes one format per run. Run it twice if you need both, and do not serve a WEBP file with a .jpg name.

tools.name: Image Converter (PNG, JPG, WEBP)
tools.summary: Batch-convert images between PNG, JPG and WEBP.
tools.description: Batch-convert PNG, JPG and WEBP images free. No sign-up and no upload: images are converted privately in your browser.
features: Convert between PNG, JPG and WEBP
No upload: runs in the browser
tools.processing: in-browser (files and text are not uploaded)
how_to: Select one or more images.
Pick the target format: PNG, JPG or WEBP.
Click Convert and download each file.

faq.q: Which format should a business actually pick?
faq.a: JPG for photographs you will upload to a marketplace, an email, or a tool that rejects newer formats. PNG when you need transparency or hard edges: logos, stamps, screenshots with text. WEBP when the image lives on a modern website and size matters. A logo exported only as a small JPEG will look soft on a retina screen and will show a box wherever the background is not white. Convert that asset to PNG or keep the SVG from the logo maker. Photographs converted to PNG get larger, not clearer.

faq.q: What happens to transparency, and what does quality 0.9 mean?
faq.a: JPG cannot store transparency. Transparent pixels are painted with the background color you pick, white by default. Set that color to your page color if the logo will sit on a tint, or do not convert that file to JPG. Quality runs from 0.1 to 1 for JPG and WEBP. 0.9 is a light touch and keeps more detail than the compressor's 75 percent default. 1 is still a lossy JPEG, not a mathematical copy. PNG ignores the quality number because it is lossless. Batch conversion uses the same format, background, and quality for every file you selected.

faq.q: Can I convert HEIC, and what fails?
faq.a: Only if the browser can decode the file. Safari often opens iPhone HEIC photos. Many desktop browsers cannot, and the page will say it could not read the image. On the phone you can set the camera to Most Compatible so new shots are JPEG, or export a JPEG from the Photos app and then convert. AVIF and some CMYK files fail the same way. Rename a .jpg that is actually a PDF and it will fail decode. The extension is not trusted; the browser has to draw the pixels.

faq.q: How do I convert a folder of product shots without mixing them up?
faq.a: Select the batch, pick JPG or WEBP, and download each result. Keep the original file name in your own folder so the SKU in the name survives. Do not convert the only copy of a transparent PNG to JPG and delete the PNG. Color shifts are possible when a wide-gamut photo is drawn to a standard canvas. For catalog work, compare one image at 100 percent zoom before you convert hundreds. There is no upload queue and no account, so a closed tab is a lost batch if you have not downloaded.

faq.q: What size should the converted file be?
faq.a: Conversion here does not resize. A 6000-pixel PNG becomes a 6000-pixel JPG, which may still be too large to email. Compress after you convert, or compress first if you already know the target width. A reasonable product image for the web is 1600 to 2000 pixels on the long side. A social avatar can be 512. Print shops often want the original pixels or a PDF, not a twice-converted JPEG. Each conversion that is lossy throws away a little more detail, so convert once from the master.

faq.q: Are the images uploaded?
faq.a: No. Decoding and encoding happen in the browser. Nothing is stored by GWB and there is no sign-up. You download each file locally. The same privacy boundary is why a failed file cannot be recovered from our side: we never had it.

faq.q: What should an invoice contain so it gets paid?
faq.a: Your legal or trade name, the client, a unique number, the invoice date, a due date, each line with quantity and price, the tax rate if any, the total, and how to pay. INV-001 is fine until you issue the next one; skipping numbers is a bookkeeping smell, duplicates are worse. A receipt is the same layout after you have been paid: switch the document type so the heading matches. This generator does not add a watermark and does not cap how many documents you make. It also does not send the invoice or reconcile the bank. Download the PDF from the print dialog by choosing Save as PDF.

faq.q: How should tax and discounts be shown?
faq.a: If you charge sales tax, the line amounts are the pre-tax price and the tax percent is applied to the subtotal. A $1,000 subtotal at 8.25 percent shows $82.50 of tax and a $1,082.50 total. Do not also bury tax inside the line price unless you say the lines are tax-inclusive, because the client and your sales-tax return will not match. This invoice form applies one tax rate to the whole document. For a mix of taxable and exempt lines, or a discount before tax, use the receipt and quote maker, which discounts first and can leave a line non-taxable, then invoice the accepted total.

faq.q: How do I keep invoice numbers and books straight?
faq.a: Store the PDF with a file name that includes the number and client. Export Excel or CSV if you want the lines in a sheet. Record income when you earn it if you are on accrual, or when you are paid if you are on cash, and be consistent. A deposit is not the full invoice: invoice the deposit or use a quote with a deposit line, then invoice the balance. Write off a bad debt in the books; do not renumber the invoice. The tool remembers nothing on a server, so your own folder is the archive.

faq.q: Can I reuse it for a receipt after payment?
faq.a: Yes. Change the document type to Receipt, keep the same line items, and save a second PDF. Use a receipt number if your sequence is separate from invoices. The payment method belongs in the notes if you need it on the face of the document; the dedicated receipt maker has a payment-method field if you want that on every copy. Do not edit a PDF you already sent in order to hide a late fee without sending a corrected invoice the client can reconcile.

faq.q: Is there a watermark, a limit, or an account?
faq.a: No watermark, no monthly cap, and no account. The page is free. PDF, Excel, and CSV exports and Send to phone run in the browser. If you want online acceptance, reminders, and a ledger, a paid invoicing product in the recommended list does that job. This page is the document itself. You are responsible for whether the tax rate and the legal name are right.

faq.q: Do client names get uploaded?
faq.a: No. Business name, client, and line items stay on the device and in the file you download. There is no GWB invoice account. Email the PDF yourself. The recommended-tool links are ordinary outbound links, labeled as partner recommendations, and they do not receive the invoice text unless you later type it into that product.

tools.name: Audio Converter & Ringtone Trimmer
tools.summary: Trim audio, add fades and export MP3 or WAV ringtones.
tools.description: Trim audio, add fade in/out and export MP3 or WAV ringtones free. No sign-up and no upload: your files never leave your device.
features: No upload: runs in the browser
tools.processing: in-browser (files and text are not uploaded)
how_to: Open an audio file from your device.
Drag the start and end sliders, and add a fade in or out.
Preview, then export as MP3 or WAV.

faq.q: MP3 or WAV, and what does this trimmer actually export?
faq.a: WAV is the uncompressed PCM of the selection, stereo or mono as in the file, at the file's own sample rate, 16-bit. It is the right export when you will edit again. MP3 is encoded in the browser at a fixed 128 kbps with the bundled LAME encoder, which is a small file and plenty for a ringtone or a voice memo. This page does not offer 192 or 320 kbps. If you need a higher-bitrate MP3, export WAV and encode elsewhere, or use the video-to-MP3 tool when the source is a video and you want 192 or 320. A one-minute stereo WAV at 44.1 kHz is about 10 MB. The same minute as 128 kbps MP3 is about 1 MB.

faq.q: How long should a ringtone or alert be, and how do fades work?
faq.a: Most phones are happy with 20 to 30 seconds. iPhone ringtone files are limited to about 30 seconds, so set the end point at or before 30 if that is the destination. A 1 to 2 second fade-out keeps the clip from clicking at the end. Fade-in can be shorter, often under a second, unless you are softening a loud attack. The fade is a gain ramp on the samples you selected, not a separate effect track. Preview before you export. The selection cannot be shorter than a tenth of a second.

faq.q: Which files open, and what if decode fails?
faq.a: The browser's audio decoder has to understand the file. MP3, WAV, M4A, AAC, OGG, and FLAC open in current browsers when the codec is supported. A file over about 200 MB is rejected so the tab does not run out of memory. If decode fails, the audio may be corrupt or use a codec the browser cannot play. Convert that file to WAV or MP3 on a machine that can play it, then trim here. The page does not download audio from a URL, a streaming site, or YouTube. It only reads a file you already have.

faq.q: What are the rights and the privacy limits?
faq.a: Trim audio you own or have a license to use. A purchased song is often licensed for personal listening, not for a remix you publish. This tool will not stop you, and it also will not fetch the song for you. Processing is local. The waveform is drawn from the samples on your device. There is no account and no upload. Export before you close the tab. Memory errors on long files are solved by a shorter selection or by exporting WAV in smaller pieces, not by sending the file to us.

faq.q: How do I make a clean clip for a podcast or a hold message?
faq.a: Set the start just before the first word and the end just after the last, then add a short fade so you do not cut a breath in half. Voice is intelligible at 128 kbps mono or stereo. Leave the original untrimmed file in your archive. Do not normalize or remove noise here; this page trims and fades only. If the level is too low, fix it in an editor before you export the master. The sample rate of the export matches the source, so a 48 kHz interview stays 48 kHz.

faq.q: Why does the MP3 sound duller than the WAV?
faq.a: 128 kbps throws away some high-frequency detail. On a phone speaker you will rarely hear it. On studio monitors, a music clip will sound tighter in the WAV. Choose WAV when the next step is editing or a master, and MP3 when the file has to be small. Re-encoding an MP3 to MP3 again makes the loss worse. Trim from WAV or from the original when you can.

tools.name: Video to MP3 Extractor
tools.summary: Pull the audio track out of your own video files as MP3 or WAV.
tools.description: Extract the audio from your own MP4, WebM or MOV videos as MP3 or WAV free. No sign-up, no upload: converted privately in your browser.
features: Extract audio from MP4, WebM or MOV
No upload: runs in the browser
tools.processing: in-browser (files and text are not uploaded)
how_to: Open a video file from your device (MP4, WebM or MOV).
Choose MP3 or WAV and a quality.
Export and download the audio file.

faq.q: Which video files work, and what do the bitrates mean?
faq.a: The browser must be able to decode the video. MP4 with AAC audio and WebM work in most current browsers. Some MOV files and HEVC or HDR phone videos do not, and the page will say it could not decode them. Export MP3 at 128 kbps for speech, 192 kbps as the default balance for music, or 320 kbps when you want the largest MP3 this page makes. WAV is lossless PCM of the decoded audio and is much larger. A five-minute stereo program at 192 kbps is about 7 MB. The same stretch as WAV at 48 kHz is on the order of 55 MB.

faq.q: Can I paste a YouTube or other link?
faq.a: No. The tool reads a video file that is already on your device. It does not accept a URL, and it is not a downloader. Use it for a screen recording, a voice memo you filmed, a project export, or other video you have the rights to use. Ripping a stream you do not own is not what this page is for and the page cannot do it. If the file will not open, export a standard H.264 MP4 with AAC audio from the app that created it and try that file.

faq.q: Why does a long video fail or stall?
faq.a: The browser decodes the audio into memory. A long, high-resolution video can exhaust a laptop or a phone even though we only keep the audio. Close other tabs, try a shorter file, or export WAV only for the section you need from a shorter source. The failure is local. There is no server-side encoder to fall back to, which is the privacy tradeoff: your video is not uploaded, so we also cannot finish the job on a bigger machine. A progress or memory message means you should use a smaller file, not refresh and hope.

faq.q: How do I get a usable voice track?
faq.a: Film or export the video with the microphone you actually want. This page does not split stems, remove music, or boost a quiet voice. 128 kbps is enough for a spoken track you will send by email. 192 kbps is a better default if the track includes music. Keep the video until you have listened to the export. Phase and sync are not an issue because you are taking the whole audio program, not relocking it to picture.

faq.q: What should I check before I publish the audio?
faq.a: Listen to the start and the end, confirm you exported the right event, and confirm you have the right to publish it. A screen recording can include notification sounds you did not mean to keep; trim those in the audio trimmer after you extract. Do not upload a client's meeting recording to a public host because the extraction was easy. The WAV is the archive copy. The MP3 is the copy you send.

faq.q: Is the video uploaded?
faq.a: No. Demuxing and encoding run in the browser. There is no account and no retained file. If the tab crashes, the video is still only on your device. Download the audio before you close the page.

tools.name: Word & Character Counter
tools.summary: Count words, characters, sentences and reading time instantly.
tools.description: Count words, characters, sentences, paragraphs and reading time instantly, free. No sign-up; your text never leaves your browser.
features: Export results to PDF, Excel (.xlsx) or CSV (in-browser)
Send to phone as a plain-text note (share, copy, .txt or QR)
tools.processing: in-browser (files and text are not uploaded)
how_to: Paste or type your text into the box.
Read the live counts for words, characters, sentences and paragraphs.
Check reading time and top keywords.

faq.q: How are words, characters, and time counted?
faq.a: Words are split on whitespace, so a hyphenated word is one word and a number is a word. Characters are shown with spaces and without them. Sentences are split on end punctuation. Paragraphs are blocks separated by blank lines. Reading time uses about 238 words per minute. Speaking time uses about 150 words per minute. A 600-word product description is about 2.5 minutes to read and about 4 minutes to read aloud. Those rates are averages for adult English, not a promise about your reader. The top-keyword list skips very common function words so you can see what you actually repeat.

faq.q: What lengths matter for real business writing?
faq.a: A search snippet is often cut near 150 to 160 characters, so write the meta description in this box and watch the character count with spaces. Many ad headlines are tighter than 30 characters. A short email people will finish is often under 200 words. A blog post that teaches something real is commonly 800 to 1,500 words, which is a reading time of roughly 4 to 7 minutes at 238 words per minute. The counter does not judge quality. It stops you from discovering the limit after you have pasted into an ad platform.

faq.q: What does keyword repetition tell you, and what does it not?
faq.a: If one product name is 8 percent of the words, the paragraph may be stuffing rather than explaining. If the name never appears, the page may be vague. The list is a frequency count, not a ranking score and not a guarantee that a search engine will treat the phrase as a topic. Proper names and SKUs count. The same word with different capitalization is grouped in the usual way the counter normalizes. Use it to edit, then read the paragraph aloud.

faq.q: How should I use it with the resume and policy tools?
faq.a: Resume bullets should usually be one or two lines, roughly 15 to 30 words. Paste a bullet here if you cannot tell whether it is bloated. Policy drafts from the policy generator run long because they have to cover topics; the counter tells you the length so you can see whether a section became a wall of text. Neither tool sends the text to the other. Copy and paste is the handoff, and it stays on the device.

faq.q: Are there limits on length?
faq.a: Very large pastes are counted locally and can take a moment. The page is built to handle a long document without uploading it. If the tab becomes slow, split the text. There is no account and no stored document. Export PDF, Excel, or CSV if you want the counts and the keyword list in a file, or send a note to your phone. The export is the counts, not a backup of a novel, unless the text is included in that export's inputs.

faq.q: Does it count HTML, code, or languages other than English?
faq.a: Tags and code are counted as they appear. A page of HTML will show a high word count that includes tags, which is not the reading length of the visible article. Paste the visible text if that is what you care about. Languages without spaces between words will not match an English word count; the character count is still meaningful. Emoji and accents count as characters. The reading-time constant is still the English average.

tools.name: Password Generator
tools.summary: Strong, random passwords generated securely on your device.
tools.description: Generate strong random passwords free with a cryptographically secure generator. No sign-up; passwords are created on your device and never stored.
tools.processing: in-browser (files and text are not uploaded)
how_to: Choose a length (16 or more is recommended).
Pick which character types to include.
Copy one of the generated passwords.

faq.q: How random is a password from this page?
faq.a: Each character is chosen with the browser's crypto.getRandomValues, which is a cryptographic generator, not Math.random. Selection is unbiased across the set you turned on. A 16-character password drawn from about 95 printable characters has on the order of 100 bits of entropy, because each character adds about 6.6 bits. Turn off symbols and you reduce the bits per character. Turn the length down to 8 and you cut the space in half in bit terms, which is a large cut, not a small one. The strength line is an entropy estimate of the settings, not a check against a list of leaked passwords.

faq.q: How long should it be, and should I reuse it?
faq.a: Use at least 12 to 16 characters for ordinary accounts and longer for email, banking, and the password manager itself. A unique password per account matters more than a clever word. Reuse means one leak opens every site that shares the password. This page does not store the password, does not put it in an export, and does not offer Send to phone, because a notes file or a QR code of a password is a copy you will forget you made. Put it in a password manager. The manager is the memory.

faq.q: What should I do with the result?
faq.a: Copy it once into the account you are creating and into the password manager. Do not email it to yourself. Do not paste it into a chat with a vendor. If a site rejects symbols, turn symbols off and add length until the strength line is still in the strong range, rather than shortening a complex password to 8 characters. A passphrase of several random words can be appropriate where you must type it often; this generator builds a random string, which is the better shape for a manager-filled login.

faq.q: What does the page refuse to do?
faq.a: It will not generate a password if every character set is off, because there is nothing to draw from. It does not invent a memorable sentence. It does not check whether a particular site's rules require a number. If a site demands a number, leave digits on. The password is shown so you can copy it. Anyone who can see your screen can see it. Generate it when you are ready to store it, then clear the page if you are on a shared machine.

faq.q: How does this compare with a website's own generator?
faq.a: A generator on a sign-up form may be fine, and it may also be a script you cannot read. This one is local and does not send the result to GWB. That does not make the password stronger than the math of its length and alphabet. A 6-character password generated perfectly is still short. Prefer this page or your manager's generator over a password built from a pet name and a year.

faq.q: Is anything stored?
faq.a: No password is written to local storage, to an export file, or to a server. There is no account. Reloading the page gives a new set. If you needed the previous one and did not save it in your manager, it is gone, which is the intended failure mode.

how_to: Add your income sources and choose whether amounts are per month, week or year.
Adjust the preset expense categories (rent, utilities, groceries and more), or add and remove your own.
Read your total income, expenses, what is left or the shortfall, each category's share of income and how you compare with the 50/30/20 rule.

faq.q: How do I apply 50/30/20 to a real take-home paycheck?
faq.a: Use monthly take-home pay, not gross salary. On $4,000 a month, needs are about $2,000, wants about $1,200, and savings or extra debt payments about $800. Needs are housing, utilities, groceries, insurance, basic transport, and minimum debt payments. Wants are eating out, subscriptions, and travel. Savings include an emergency fund and retirement contributions beyond a payroll 401(k) that already left the paycheck. If rent alone is $1,800, the 50 percent needs band is already tight; the rule is a checkpoint, not a reason to skip rent. The calculator tags each category and shows how far you are from those shares.

faq.q: Should the income box be gross, and how do weekly bills convert?
faq.a: Type take-home pay. A biweekly net of $1,690.85 is not $3,381.70 every month. $1,690.85 times 26 divided by 12 is $3,663.51 as a monthly average. Enter that monthly average, or enter the check and tell the tool the amount is per paycheck period it offers (month, week, or year) so it annualizes consistently. faq.q: What does a shortfall mean for the next month?
faq.a: If expenses exceed income, the result is a shortfall, not a remaining balance you can spend. Cut wants first, then renegotiate a need you control, such as a phone plan, before you cut a minimum debt payment. A one-month shortfall covered by savings should be labeled a transfer from savings, not new income, or next month's plan will assume the transfer repeats. The percent-of-income column shows which single category is doing the damage. A category over 100 percent of income is a data error or a bill that belongs in a different month.

faq.q: How do I use this with irregular freelance income?
faq.a: Budget a baseline month from your lowest reliable month, and put surplus months into a tax and slow-month reserve rather than into wants. Self-employed people should treat the tax reserve as a need. If the freelance rate calculator says you should set aside 25 percent, that transfer is not optional spending. Annual expenses such as insurance can be entered as a yearly amount so the month you pay them does not look like a crisis and the other months do not look richer than they are.

faq.q: Is the budget saved on a server?
faq.a: Only if you tick Remember my budget on this device. That copy lives in this browser's local storage and is never uploaded. Untick it to delete it. Another browser or phone will not see it. Export PDF, Excel, or CSV when you want a copy you control, or send a plain-text note to your phone. There is no account. Anyone who uses this browser profile can open the saved budget, so do not use Remember on a shared computer.

faq.q: How often should I revise the plan?
faq.a: Redo it when take-home pay changes, when a rent or insurance bill changes, and at least once a quarter. A budget that matched January will lie in December if annual gifts and insurance were never entered. The 50/30/20 comparison is a guide for consumer cash flow. A business with inventory should also track gross margin on the profit margin calculator and keep business and household money in separate columns so a good sales month does not look like personal spending money.

faq.q: Which 2026 figures does this calculator use?
faq.a: Federal brackets and standard deductions follow IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-32 for tax year 2026, including the inflation adjustments described in the IRS newsroom note on the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. The standard deduction used here is $16,100 single or married filing separately, $32,200 married filing jointly, and $24,150 head of household. Social Security is 6.2 percent of wages up to the 2026 wage base of $184,500. Medicare is 1.45 percent of all wages, plus the 0.9 percent Additional Medicare Tax on wages above $200,000 single or head of household, $250,000 married filing jointly, or $125,000 married filing separately. Employee 401(k) deferrals are capped in the model at the 2026 elective deferral limit of $24,500. State brackets, standard deductions, and personal exemptions or credits follow the Tax Foundation compilation of state individual income tax rates and brackets for 2026. We re-check those published tables when we update the tax year and do not invent rates.

faq.q: Walk me through an $80,000 single filer in Texas.
faq.a: Texas has no wage income tax in this model. Gross wages $80,000 minus the $16,100 standard deduction leaves $63,900 of federal taxable income. Tax is $1,240 on the first $12,400 at 10 percent, $4,560 on the next $38,000 at 12 percent, and $2,970 on the remaining $13,500 at 22 percent, which is $8,770 of federal income tax. Social Security is $80,000 times 0.062 = $4,960. Medicare is $80,000 times 0.0145 = $1,160. Combined tax is $14,890, so take-home pay is $65,110 before any benefit premiums. The marginal federal rate on the next dollar is 22 percent, but the effective rate on gross pay is 18.61 percent because of the standard deduction, the lower brackets, and payroll taxes. A pre-tax 401(k) of $5,000 stays inside the 22 percent bracket and lowers federal income tax by exactly $1,100, to $7,670. Payroll taxes do not fall, because 401(k) deferrals are still FICA wages. Cash in hand becomes $61,210, and $5,000 sits in the retirement account.

faq.q: How is a state with a flat tax different, such as Georgia?
faq.a: Georgia's 2026 table in this tool is a flat 5.19 percent after a standard deduction of $12,000 single or $24,000 married filing jointly, with no personal exemption in the simplified table. On $80,000 of single wages the state tax is (80,000 minus 12,000) times 0.0519 = $3,529.20. Federal income tax and FICA stay the same as the Texas example, so total tax is about $18,419 and take-home pay is about $61,581. States with graduated brackets, exemptions, or credits will not match a flat percentage of gross pay. The calculator applies the state's standard deduction and, where the Tax Foundation table records one, a personal exemption or credit. It does not apply city taxes, school-district taxes, or state disability insurance such as California SDI.

faq.q: What does the calculator leave out on purpose?
faq.a: It estimates wage income only. It does not apply the Child Tax Credit, Earned Income Credit, education credits, itemized deductions, the qualified business income deduction, capital gains, unemployment, or local wage taxes. Head of household and married filing separately use the published schedules in the engine; they are not a substitute for a return that has dependents or community-property rules. Self-employed people also owe self-employment tax of 15.3 percent on 92.35 percent of net earnings, half of which is deductible, and they usually make quarterly estimates. Use the freelance rate calculator for pricing and a tax professional or the IRS withholding estimator before you change a W-4. Washington taxes certain capital gains but not wages, so this tool shows zero state income tax on wages there.

faq.q: How should a small business use the result in its books?
faq.a: Compare the federal income tax, state income tax, Social Security, and Medicare lines with a recent pay stub before you rely on the annual figure. If you are an S corporation owner, wages and distributions are not the same number: only reasonable compensation runs through this wage calculator. Sole proprietors should not type profit into the salary box and treat the result as their full tax. Record employee withholdings as liabilities until you deposit them. When you export PDF, Excel, or CSV, the file is built in the browser and labeled as a 2026 estimate, not a filing. Nothing is written to a GWB account because there is no account. Save results downloads a PDF, Excel workbook, or CSV that you generate locally, or Send to phone shares a plain-text note. faq.a: Body text needs a contrast ratio of at least 4.5 to 1 against its background under ordinary WCAG rules, and large text needs at least 3 to 1. faq.a: Straight time is hourly rate times hours per week times weeks worked. A $25 rate at 40 hours and 52 weeks is $52,000 a year, $1,000 a week, and $4,333.33 a month before tax. faq.q: What does a $25-an-hour single paycheck look like in Texas?
faq.a: Gross is $52,000. Federal taxable income after the 2026 standard deduction of $16,100 is $35,900. Tax is $1,240 plus 12 percent of $23,500, which is $2,820, for $4,060 of federal income tax. Social Security is $3,224 and Medicare is $754. Take-home pay for the year is $43,962 before health insurance or other deductions, or about $1,690.85 on each of 26 biweekly checks. The same gross paid semimonthly is 24 checks of about $1,831.75. Weekly is 52 checks of about $845.42. The annual tax does not change with frequency; only the size of each check does.

faq.q: Why is biweekly different from twice a month?
faq.a: Biweekly means every two weeks, 26 pays in a normal year and 27 pays in some calendar years when a payday falls on January 1 or a leap pattern adds a check. Semimonthly means the 15th and the last day, always 24 pays. People who budget monthly often multiply a biweekly check by two and then feel short in the two months that have three checks. Multiply the biweekly net by 26 and divide by 12 to see a true monthly average. This calculator uses 26, 52, 24, or 12 exactly, and it does not move holidays to the previous business day.

faq.q: Which taxes come out, and which do not?

Health insurance, HSA contributions, garnishments, union dues, local taxes, and state paid-leave or disability premiums are not deducted. A W-2 employee should not also subtract self-employment tax. If you are both an owner and an employee, run wages here and estimate profit separately.

faq.q: How do I check the result against a pay stub?
faq.a: Divide the year-to-date Social Security on a stub by 0.062. That implied wage base should be close to year-to-date gross if you are under $184,500 and have no pre-tax cafeteria plan that is exempt from FICA. faq.q: What is the difference between margin and markup on a $40 cost and a $65 price?
faq.a: Profit is $25. Margin is profit divided by the selling price: 25 divided by 65 = 38.46 percent. Markup is profit divided by cost: 25 divided by 40 = 62.5 percent. A 50 percent markup on a $40 cost is a $60 price and only a 33.33 percent margin, because 20 divided by 60 is one third. Quoting markup when a buyer asked for margin is a common way to underprice. This page shows both from the same two numbers so you can answer either question without converting in your head.

faq.q: How do I set a price from a target margin, and what is a simple ROI check?
faq.a: Price equals cost divided by 1 minus the target margin. A 40 percent margin on a $40 cost is 40 divided by 0.60 = $66.67. The same cost at a 40 percent markup is 40 times 1.40 = $56.00, which is only a 28.6 percent margin. A simple return on the inventory dollar, sometimes called markup ROI, is profit divided by cost, which is the markup itself: $26.67 profit on $66.67 is a 66.7 percent return on the $40 cost, not a 40 percent return. If you also spend $10 of shipping and fees that are not in cost, put them in cost before you divide or the margin will not survive the order.

faq.q: How many units cover $5,000 of fixed costs?
faq.a: Break-even units equal fixed costs divided by price minus variable cost per unit, rounded up to a whole unit. At a $25 price and a $10 variable cost, contribution is $15. $5,000 divided by 15 is 333.33, so you need 334 units. Revenue at that point is 334 times $25 = $8,350. Contribution margin ratio is 15 divided by 25 = 60 percent. To clear an extra $3,000 profit goal, divide 8,000 by 15 and round up to 534 units. If price is not above variable cost, there is no break-even: every sale loses money.

faq.q: How should a product business use margin in its books?
faq.a: Gross margin in the accounts is net sales minus cost of goods sold, divided by net sales. Cost of goods includes the unit you typed plus inbound freight and packaging if you cannot sell without them. Payment processing, marketplace fees, and discounts are often outside the unit cost people type here. A 38 percent calculator margin can become a 20 percent accounting margin after a 15 percent discount and a 3 percent card fee. Run the price on the discounted net and put the fee in variable cost. faq.a: Use the four-in-one business calculators page for a fast margin, a single sales-tax line, a loan payment, or a monthly break-even while you are in a meeting. faq.a: It is a planning reserve, not a filed return. US self-employed people generally pay self-employment tax of 15.3 percent on 92.35 percent of net profit, plus federal income tax and often state income tax. On $80,000 of net profit, self-employment tax alone is about $11,304 before the deduction for half of it. A 25 to 35 percent combined reserve is a common planning range, but a high-earning filer in a high-tax state can need more, and a low-profit year can need less. faq.q: UPC-A, EAN-13, Code 128, or QR: which one goes on the product?
faq.a: Use UPC-A for a retail product sold in the United States or Canada when you have a GS1-licensed number. UPC-A is 12 digits, and the last digit is a check digit this tool can compute. Use EAN-13 for international retail; it is 13 digits with its own check digit. Use Code 128 for your own SKUs, bin labels, and packing slips. Code 128 carries letters and numbers and does not require GS1, but a retailer will not treat a homemade Code 128 as a UPC. Use QR for a URL or a longer note, not for a POS barcode the scanner at a grocery lane expects to be a UPC.

faq.q: Can I invent a UPC?
faq.a: You can draw a symbol that is mathematically valid, including the check digit, from any 11 digits you type. Selling that symbol as if it were your licensed UPC is how you collide with another company's product in a retailer's system. License the number from GS1 US or the GS1 office in your country, then type the number they assigned. Internal warehouse labels should use Code 128 and a prefix you control, such as SKU-10042, so they are obviously not retail UPCs. The tool validates the check digit. It does not validate ownership.

faq.q: How do I print Avery-style sheets so they line up?
faq.a: Download the label sheet PDF and print at 100 percent or Actual size on US Letter. Do not use Fit to page, which scales the sheet and walks the codes off the labels. Avery 5160 is 30 labels, 2.625 by 1 inch. Avery 5163 is 10 labels, 4 by 2 inches, which is easier to scan. Avery 5167 is 80 labels, 1.75 by 0.5 inches, which is tight for anything but a short code. Print a proof on plain paper and hold it against a label sheet in the light before you use the real stock. Leave the human-readable digits on unless you have a reason to hide them.

faq.q: What makes a code fail at the scanner?
faq.a: Quiet zone too small, bars too thin because the PDF was scaled, lamination glare, a color other than black on white, or a code printed on a curved bottle at a size that is too small. Thermal printers want a high-contrast image and a size the print head can hold. If you use a thermal printer, a single-label PNG or SVG at a known size is often easier than a Letter sheet. Test with the same scanner you will use at the counter, not only with a phone. A phone can read a QR that a laser POS scanner will ignore.

faq.q: How should the text file of codes be prepared?
faq.a: One code per line. Optionally add a product name and a price separated by vertical bars: SKU-10042 | Blue mug | $14.00. The name and price print on the label. They are not encoded into a UPC, which can only hold the digits. Copies multiplies each line on the sheet. Export CSV or Excel if you want a manifest of what you printed. The PDF is the print file. Keep the text list so you can reprint without retyping.

faq.q: Are the codes uploaded?
faq.a: No. Barcodes are drawn in the browser with the self-hosted library, and the PDF is built locally. There is no account and no registry of your SKUs. A retail UPC is still a public number once you print it on a product. The privacy of the file is separate from the secrecy of a number you put on a shelf.

tools.description: Calculate sales tax for any US state with 2026 state and average local rates. Reverse sales tax from a total, multiple items, non-taxable lines. Free, instant, no sign-up.
features: 2026 state and average local rates for all 50 states and DC
Reverse sales tax: find the pre-tax price from a total
Non-taxable lines (for example gift cards or exempt goods)
Custom exact rate for your city or county
Compare tax on the same purchase across every state
Export results to PDF, Excel (.xlsx) or CSV (in-browser)
Send to phone as a plain-text note (share, copy, .txt or QR)
tools.processing: in-browser (files and text are not uploaded)
how_to: Pick your state and the rate to use. For an exact rate, choose "My exact rate" and enter the combined rate from your receipt or your state revenue department.
Choose whether the prices you enter are before tax or already include tax.
List the items with quantity and price, untick "Taxable" for any exempt item, and read the tax and total.

faq.q: How do I add sales tax, with a real receipt example?
faq.a: Tax equals the taxable amount times the rate as a decimal. At a combined 8.25 percent, tax on $100.00 is $8.25 and the customer pays $108.25. On three taxable items of $24.00, $10.50, and $6.00 the taxable base is $40.50 and the tax is $3.34125, which you should round to the cent the way your state requires, usually $3.34, for a total of $43.84. This tool rounds money to the cent on line amounts and on the tax result. If one line is a gift card or a labor charge your state exempts, untick Taxable so it stays in the total but out of the tax base.

faq.q: How do I remove tax that is already in the price?
faq.a: Divide the tax-inclusive total by 1 plus the rate. A shelf price of $108.25 at 8.25 percent is $108.25 divided by 1.0825 = $100.00 before tax, so the embedded tax is $8.25. A $249.99 total at the same rate is $249.99 divided by 1.0825 = $230.94 before tax and $19.05 of tax, after cent rounding. Choose Tax included in the tool when the number on the tag already contains tax. Do not also multiply that tag price by the rate or you will tax the tax.

faq.q: Why does my city's rate differ from the state average?
faq.a: The state rate in the table is the statewide rate. The local figure is a population-weighted average of city, county, and special-district rates published by the Tax Foundation as of July 1, 2026, not the rate at one address. Texas, for example, is 6.25 percent state plus about 1.95 percent average local, or 8.20 percent combined, but a specific city can be higher or lower. Alaska, Delaware, Montana, New Hampshire, and Oregon have no statewide sales tax; Alaska's local average is about 1.82 percent. Choose My exact rate and type the combined rate from your state's rate lookup or from a recent receipt when you are charging a customer.

faq.q: What should a shop record for sales tax payable?
faq.a: Sales tax you collect is not revenue. Book the pre-tax price as sales and the tax as a liability until you remit it. If you give a discount, this tool follows the usual US order: discount reduces the subtotal, then tax is computed on the discounted taxable amount. Exempt sales still belong in gross receipts if your state return asks for them, but they are not in the tax you owe. Use the compare-by-state table only to see how the same basket changes across states. It is not a nexus study. Shipping, freight, and digitally delivered goods are taxable in some states and not others, so confirm the category before you file.

faq.q: How do state and average local rates get updated?
faq.a: Rates in the menu come from the Tax Foundation 2026 sales tax rates midyear update, rates as of July 1, 2026, with state rates cross-checked against the Foundation's state sales tax table. We do not scrape a live rate API at the moment you calculate, which is why an exact city rate belongs in My exact rate. When a state changes its rate, the published table and this page are updated together. The page states the as-of date next to the source link. Food, clothing, and services can be taxed at a different rate or exempt even when the general rate is correct.

faq.q: Is the basket I type sent to a server?
faq.a: No. Items, quantities, prices, and the rate are processed in the page. You can export the result as PDF, Excel, or CSV, or send a plain-text note to your phone, all created in the browser. There is no account. The rate source link goes to the Tax Foundation; following it leaves this site and is covered by their policy, not by a data upload of your basket.
